essay.title: THEORY
essay.instruction: Answer the required number of questions. Show all necessary workings clearly.

questions.question:
(a) Without using mathematical tables, find log₁₀6 + log₁₀45 − log₁₀27.
(b) Solve 8ˣ = 32.
(c) Simplify the given index expression, showing all steps.

(a) For the matrix A supplied, calculate 2A² − 3A + 4I₂.
(b) Solve the given determinant equation for y.

(a) Solve (3x+2) = ¾(2x−3).
(b) Find the equation of the line passing through A(−2,7) and B(2,−3).

(a) A town's population increases by 4% each year. If its population is 42,500, find the population four years later.
(b) Ali, Musa and Yusuf share ₦420,000 in the ratio 3:5:8. Find the sum of Ali's and Yusuf's shares.
The masses (kg) of logs are grouped as 31–40, 41–50, 51–60, 61–70, 71–80, 81–90 with frequencies 3, 10, 15, 12, 6, 4. Calculate the mean, mode and median.
The first and last terms of an AP are 5 and 89 respectively, and the sum is 611. Find (i) the number of terms and (ii) the common difference.
P varies directly as Q and inversely as R². If P=1 when Q=8 and R=2, find Q when P=3 and R=5.

A cone has slant height 10.5 cm and curved surface area 115.5 cm². Calculate, correct to 3 significant figures, (i) the base radius, (ii) the height and (iii) the volume. Take π=22/7. Also find the perimeter of an arc sector of radius 7 cm and angle 120°.

An aircraft flies from P(12°N,11°W) to Q(12°N,11°E), then to S(44°N,11°E). Using R=6400 km and π=3.142, calculate the total distance, average speed if the first leg takes 2 h and the second 6 h, and the time difference between Q and S.
Given log₁₀2=0.3010 and log₁₀3=0.4771, evaluate (i) log₁₀12 and (ii) log₁₀15. Also solve (y−1)log₁₀4 = ylog₁₀16 without a calculator.
With ruler and compasses only, construct a parallelogram ABCD with AB=8 cm, ∠BAC=45° and ∠ABC=60°. Measure BC. Locate P inside triangle ABC such that PA=PB and PC=4 cm, then measure PD.

Marks (%) 0–9,10–19,20–29,30–39,40–49,50–59,60–69,70–79,80–89,90–99 have frequencies 7,11,17,20,29,34,30,25,21,6. Construct a cumulative frequency table and ogive. Use it to estimate the distinction cut-off if the top 5% earned distinction and the probability that a randomly selected candidate scored at most 45%.
